assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes
daemon_capability: full (for the scenario's actual recordable recipe — two ordinary `muse` REPL launches)
driver_capability: gap:start_session
→ route: **driver-gap** — record ports start_session/session from a slot-model sibling driver (codex/gemini-cli/pi; `_lib/drive/slots.sh` is already sourced and wired) before driving.

## Agent pillar

`muse` is a bash wrapper that `exec`s a version-pinned native binary (muse-bin-<ver>-R<build>) — `exec` replaces the process image, so one invocation is exactly one OS process (format-spec §2, confirmed via `file`/`grep exec` on the wrapper). format-spec §2 live-drove two plain `muse --provider echo` interactive sessions on this machine (no `serve`) and confirmed each minted a dedicated, unshared PID (38088, 39923), each holding exactly one `.session.lock` fd — directly demonstrating the scenario's premise (two concurrent same-cwd sessions) is trivially supported as-shipped.

## Daemon pillar — session identity and PID binding for the recordable path

Each session gets its own directory `~/.local/share/muse/sessions/<YYYY>/<MM>/<DD>/<session-uuid>/session.jsonl` (format-spec §1). `core/adapters/inbound/agents/muse/adapter.go`'s `sessionIDFromPath` (lines 145-159) derives the session_id from the transcript's parent directory basename, validated against a UUID-shaped regex so a date component or the `sessions` root itself can never mint a phantom session — cwd plays no role in session identity, so two sessions sharing a cwd are structurally distinct rows regardless of PID. `agent.go`'s `Source()` wires `agent.JSONLineParser{NewParser: func() agent.LineParser { return &Parser{} }}` — a FRESH stateful `Parser{}` per transcript file, so two same-cwd sessions never share parser state (the identical isolation shape claudecode's own 4-1 assessment cites and that this repo has already proven correct for that adapter).

**PID binding — the daemon correctly handles the "interesting" shared-process case, at the discovery layer.** `pid.go`'s own doc comment states the design directly: this is deliberately NOT a process-name+cwd scan (junie/vibe's shape), because format-spec §2 caught a LIVE example of `muse serve` (Meta's MSP session-host subcommand) where ONE OS pid (66997) held open flock file descriptors on 11 DIFFERENT sessions' `.session.lock` files simultaneously — "one muse-bin pid ⇒ one session" is false for muse. `DiscoverPID` instead asks, per session, "who holds THIS session's own `.session.lock` open" via `processlifecycle.DiscoverPIDByTranscriptWriter` — an lsof-style writer lookup, the SAME already-tested primitive codex/pi use (dedicated coverage: `processlifecycle/writerof_mode_test.go`). Because the lookup is scoped to one session's own lock path, the answer is correct whether that session runs as a dedicated interactive invocation or shares a host pid with ten others — no election/disambiguation among candidates is needed (contrast junie's process-sidecar binding, which needs a newest-startedAt election among several sidecars naming the same pid).

The adapter also deliberately does NOT trust the transcript's own embedded `route_facts.pid` field (present on the wire: `{"payload_type":"runtime.session.route_facts","payload":{"record":{"cwd":...,"pid":66997,...}}}`, format-spec §2) — and format-spec proved this field UNRELIABLE for the shared-host case: of the 11 sessions sharing pid 66997, only ONE actually recorded `route_facts.pid:66997` in its own log (the field appears to be written once at host-bind time, not per-session-load). `parseRouteFacts` (parser.go:589-595) reads only `cwd` from this payload and never touches `pid` — confirmed by grep, no other reference to route_facts's pid field exists anywhere in the adapter. Trusting the embedded field instead of the lock-file lookup would have silently misattributed 10 of 11 sessions; the adapter avoids that correctly.

So for two ordinary same-cwd `muse` launches (the scenario's actual process, and what this cell's driver produces): distinct session_ids (directory-derived), independent parser state (fresh `Parser{}` per file), and correct/independent PID bindings (per-session lock-file lsof lookup, proven to return the two DIFFERENT dedicated pids format-spec §2 measured) — no cross-contamination surface.

## A confirmed daemon architectural gap, one layer up — real, but NOT reached by this cell's recordable recipe

The task brief calls the shared-process (`muse serve`) case "the interesting one," so I traced it up from pid.go's discovery layer into the daemon's cross-adapter PID reconciliation layer, `core/application/services/pid_manager.go`, and found a genuine, currently-shipping bug there — confirmed by an existing PASSING test, not inferred:

`assignPIDLocked` (pid_manager.go:759-797) and `cleanupStalePIDHolders` (pid_manager.go:724-757) enforce a GLOBAL, cross-adapter invariant, in the doc comment's own words: "A non-subagent PID can only belong to one session at a time, so a session claiming a PID makes any other non-subagent holder of that PID stale." When `HandlePIDAssigned(pid, sessionID)` finds another non-subagent session already holding that same pid, it is marked stale and `cleanupStalePIDHolders` DELETES it outright (`pm.repo.Delete(old.SessionID)`, broadcasting `PushTypeDeleted`) — proven live by `TestHandlePIDAssigned_FiresSupersededHook` (pid_manager_test.go:1256-1287): two independent session rows ("old","new") sharing one PID, and the test explicitly asserts the OLD row is deleted once the new one claims the PID (`if repo.states["old"] != nil { t.Fatal(...) }`).

This logic was built for a real, different pattern (the doc comment names it: "the /clear pattern, where the same process starts a new transcript under a new UUID" — a genuine supersession, one session replacing another on the SAME still-alive process). Muse's `muse serve` host mode falsifies the invariant's universal premise: multiple TOP-LEVEL, simultaneously-alive, UNRELATED sessions can legitimately and permanently share one pid (11 at once, per format-spec §2), none superseding any other. If a recipe drove `muse serve` with two concurrently-hosted client sessions, the second session's `HandlePIDAssigned` call would DELETE the first session's row entirely — not a wrong-PID display, a session vanishing from the dashboard, which would fail this exact scenario's "two distinct session rows appear ... does not cross-contaminate" acceptance criteria outright.

**Why this stays a caveat, not `daemon=bug`, for THIS cell:** `muse serve` is a stdio-owned MSP host (`muse --help`: "the client owns this process's stdin/stdout and is its only connection", cited in format-spec §2) — a fundamentally different invocation shape than the TUI keypress-driven interactive REPL this scenario's driver (and every sibling adapter's 4-1 recipe) uses. `driver-interactive.sh`'s `launch_repl` runs plain `muse --trust-workspace` under tmux, never `muse serve`; two such launches get dedicated PIDs (proven above), so THIS cell's actual recording will never contain the buggy trace — asserting `daemon=bug` would describe an event this recording cannot produce, which the assess rules flag as exactly the wrong call for a narrow, unreached gap. Per the Vacuous-pass rule I am instead naming this explicitly rather than silently: a green recording of this cell proves nothing about the muse-serve shared-host case. That would need its own recipe (a stdio MSP client driver, which the current tmux-keypress driver architecture cannot produce) and is a real, separate, worth-flagging daemon defect once such a driver exists.

## Driver pillar

`start_session`/`session` are stubbed `not_implemented` in `replaydata/agents/muse/driver-interactive.sh` (the case-statement arms are present per the #496 scaffold convention, but `DRIVE_ELICITS="send slash wait_turn sleep exit_clean"` does not list them) — confirmed directly by running `driver_elicits_from_file` against the driver, which returns exactly that 5-primitive set, so `recipe-lint`'s semantic check flags a recipe using `start_session`/`session` as a `semantic_gap`. The shared `_lib/drive/slots.sh` multi-session bookkeeping (`alloc_slot`/`load_slot`/`save_active`) is already sourced and wired in this driver, matching the exact shape `record` needs to port `start_session` from a sibling slot-model driver (codex/gemini-cli/pi), per the #666 precedent cited in the driver's own header comment.
caveats: MUSE-SERVE SHARED-PID BUG (load-bearing, see body): pid_manager.go's cross-adapter same-PID reconciliation (assignPIDLocked/cleanupStalePIDHolders) assumes a non-subagent PID belongs to at most one session — proven false for muse's `muse serve` host mode (11 sessions, 1 pid, format-spec §2) and proven to DELETE the older session's row when violated (TestHandlePIDAssigned_FiresSupersededHook, pid_manager_test.go:1256). This is real and would fail this scenario's acceptance criteria if the shared-host mode were exercised, but this cell's tmux-keypress driver structurally cannot drive `muse serve` (a stdio MSP host, not a TUI), so the recordable recipe never reaches it. Kept as daemon=full for THIS cell rather than daemon=bug because the bug describes a trace this recording will not contain; flagging prominently rather than silently per the Vacuous-pass rule.

route_facts.pid is present on the wire (runtime.session.route_facts.record.pid) but proven unreliable for shared-host sessions — only 1 of 11 sessions sharing a host pid actually recorded that true value (format-spec §2). The adapter correctly never reads it (parseRouteFacts only extracts cwd); noted so a future change doesn't 'simplify' PID discovery by switching to the transcript-embedded field.

UNVERIFIED, carried forward from the format-spec: whether nested subagent session directories (<parent>/subagent/<child>/session.jsonl) have their own .session.lock. pid.go's fallback (retry DiscoverPIDByTranscriptWriter against the transcript file itself) covers this uniformly if they do not, but format-spec §9 never directly inspected a subagent directory's file listing for a lock file — its listing evidence only confirmed session.jsonl entries. Not exercised by this scenario's top-level-only recipe, so it does not affect this cell's verdict.

No dollar-cost field is ever persisted in session.jsonl — format-spec §6 ran a strict JSON-key scan (not substring) across all 48 session/approval-review files in the corpus and found zero cost-keyed records. muse's model id ('muse-spark-1.3-contributor') has no entry in core/pkg/capacity/aliases.go (grepped directly, no match), so EstimatedCostUSD will compute as zero/unknown for a live recording under the current pricing table. The spec therefore asserts cost_nonzero: false. Tokens ARE durably persisted (model_completed.usage with real input/output counts, format-spec §6) and are mapped into ev.Tokens by parser.go:395-421, so tokens_nonzero: true is asserted.

Generic proc-<PID> presession scanning (processlifecycle.Scanner, wired UNCONDITIONALLY for every adapter in cmd/irrlichd/wiring.go:103-114 regardless of Source variant) applies to muse too, since muse declares a CommandPattern Process.Match. The spec anchors each session's birth phase on its first WORKING transition (never ready), following claudecode's/pi's/mistral-vibe's proven pattern for exactly this reason — a proc-<PID> placeholder row is born ready and never transitions to working, so anchoring on working cannot bind to it.

Recipe ordering is load-bearing: session 1's first wait_turn (which resolves and CACHES its TRANSCRIPT) must complete before start_session launches session 2. muse-driver-audit.md documents a live-reproduced hazard (item 3) where resolve_transcript's `find ... -newer $MARKER | sort | tail -n1` can resolve to a concurrent, unrelated session's transcript if called before the first is cached — the audit explicitly notes the shipped `-not -path subagent` fix 'does not fully solve races against concurrent, unrelated top-level sessions.' The recipe below follows the same safe ordering already proven for claudecode/pi/mistral-vibe (send→wait_turn→sleep→start_session), which keeps session 1's resolution outside that race window entirely.

This recipe launches plain `muse` (never `muse serve`); it assumes no ambient MSP host silently reattaches a driven invocation to a shared pid instead of minting a dedicated one. Not directly tested either way — format-spec §2's dedicated-pid measurement was taken with no muse serve host running — so this is named as an environment precondition rather than asserted safe under all conditions.

sources.note: Source(): FilesUnderRoot with SessionIDFromPath/ParentSessionIDFromPath + JSONLineParser{NewParser: fresh &Parser{} per file}; Agent()'s doc comment states the 1-PID-can-serve-many-sessions rationale for keying DiscoverPID off each session's own lock file rather than a name/cwd scan.
sessionIDFromPath (lines 145-159): session id = session.jsonl's parent directory basename, validated against a UUID regex; cwd plays no role in identity.

DiscoverPID's full doc comment: format-spec §2's 11-sessions-on-1-pid finding is cited directly as the reason this keys off each session's own .session.lock via processlifecycle.DiscoverPIDByTranscriptWriter rather than a process-name+cwd scan.

parseRouteFacts (lines 589-595) reads only cwd, never pid, from runtime.session.route_facts — deliberately avoiding the field format-spec §2 proved unreliable for shared-host sessions. parseUsage (lines 395-421) maps model_completed.usage into ev.Tokens (real, non-zero for any live turn); no cost field is ever parsed (none exists on the wire, format-spec §6).
DiscoverPIDByTranscriptWriter (line 254): the shared lsof-style WriterOf primitive muse's pid.go calls, already used and tested for codex/pi (processlifecycle/writerof_mode_test.go).

assignPIDLocked (759-797) / cleanupStalePIDHolders (724-757): the cross-adapter 'a PID belongs to at most one non-subagent session' invariant, and its doc-commented rationale (the /clear supersession pattern) — the mechanism that would delete one row in muse's shared-host case, per this cell's caveats.

TestHandlePIDAssigned_FiresSupersededHook (line 1256): live proof that two independent non-subagent sessions sharing one PID results in the OLDER session's row being deleted — the concrete evidence behind the muse-serve caveat, not a guess.

buildAgentWatchers (lines 78-116): processlifecycle.NewScanner is wired unconditionally for every adapter (any Source variant) and configured with the adapter's CommandPattern (lines 103-106) — confirms muse also gets generic proc-<PID> presession scanning, motivating the working-anchored spec phases.

DRIVE_ELICITS="send slash wait_turn sleep exit_clean" (confirmed via driver_elicits_from_file) omits start_session/session, whose dispatch-loop arms call not_implemented; _lib/drive/slots.sh is already sourced (alloc_slot/load_slot/save_active present), the exact shape record needs to port the missing primitives from a sibling slot-model driver.

§1 (session identity: directory-basename id, UUID pattern), §2 (process binding: dedicated pid per plain invocation vs 11-sessions-on-1-pid under muse serve, route_facts.pid unreliability), §6 (tokens durably persisted, no cost field anywhere in a 48-file corpus scan), §7 (model identity fields).

Item 3 (transcript-resolution seam): live-reproduced race where resolve_transcript can pick a concurrent/unrelated session's transcript; explicitly notes the shipped fix does not fully solve races against concurrent, unrelated top-level sessions — the basis for this cell's recipe-ordering caveat.
Template recipe/spec structure (send/wait_turn/sleep/start_session/re-drive session 1) and the working-anchor-over-ready pattern to dodge a proc-<PID> presession row, reused here.
Grepped for muse/meta/spark — no entry, confirming the cost_nonzero:false caveat (no pricing table match for muse-spark-1.3-contributor).

preconditions: muse CLI on PATH and authenticated (muse login, or META_API_KEY exported)
irrlichd is recording — run-cell.sh isolated mode (spawns its own --record daemon on 7837), or --attach against a daemon started with --record

no `muse serve` host process is running that could reattach a driven invocation to a shared pid instead of minting a dedicated one — UNVERIFIED whether this could even happen (format-spec §2's dedicated-pid measurement had no serve host running), named as a precondition rather than assumed safe
record ports start_session and session from a slot-model sibling driver (codex/gemini-cli/pi) before this recipe can run — DRIVE_ELICITS currently omits both
setup: Driver auto-starts session 1 (slot 1) via `tmux new-session ... muse --trust-workspace` in <staging>/cwd; the session directory materializes under ~/.local/share/muse/sessions/<Y>/<M>/<D>/<uuid>/ and is resolved by resolve_transcript's marker-based find (excluding subagent/)
The start_session step (once ported) launches session 2 (slot 2) in the SAME <staging>/cwd; --trust-workspace means no repeated trust-modal wait for the second launch
Steps carrying {"session":1} route send/wait_turn back to session 1 while session 2 stays alive, exercising the concurrent, independent arcs

verify: events.jsonl contains 2 distinct session-directory UUIDs, both keyed to the same cwd
each UUID has its own independent working->ready arc; no transition on one UUID is attributed to the other

no state flapping: the daemon never swaps the PID-to-session binding between the two rows (each session's own .session.lock lsof lookup should return its own dedicated pid, per format-spec §2)
the two PIDs are DIFFERENT (dedicated-pid case, not the muse-serve shared-host case) — if they come back equal, re-check for a stray muse serve host and re-record
